description: Christmas and celebrity episodes open a run that moves through art, animation, astronomy, radioactivity, international institutions, Viennese food, classical music, Venice, cosmology and Roman history.

s04e01.description: Art and public monuments reach one of their less dignified moments when a young boy urinating becomes legitimate quiz material. Christmas television rarely receives a more efficient reminder that Millionaire can make absolutely anything academically relevant.

s04e02.description: Wallace and Gromit bring stop-motion charm to the question ladder, where even beloved animation is fair game for exact recall. The episode bounces between popular culture and broader trivia without allowing familiarity to become comfort.

s04e03.description: The scale of the universe becomes quiz material through astronomical distances. Cosmic numbers and earthly general knowledge share the same ladder, making the episode a neat demonstration that both the very large and the very trivial can be equally troublesome.

s04e04.description: Radioactivity gives the episode a scientific glow, strictly metaphorical and therefore considerably safer. Physics and general knowledge meet on a ladder where invisible phenomena are somehow easier to discuss than the visible four options on screen.

s04e05.description: UNESCO turns an international acronym into the episode’s memorable knowledge checkpoint. Institutions, culture and assorted trivia share the ladder, with the familiar quiz-show lesson that recognising an abbreviation is not remotely the same as expanding it correctly.

s04e06.description: Vienna’s Sachertorte supplies a rich slice of culinary trivia. Food becomes serious business for a moment before the ladder moves elsewhere, leaving behind the useful discovery that cake knowledge can apparently sit comfortably beside history and science.

s04e07.description: Beethoven’s Eroica Symphony brings heroic musical ambition to the hot seat. Classical culture anchors an otherwise varied question set, and the episode briefly suggests civilisation is progressing before another multiple-choice dilemma restores normality.

s04e08.description: A Venetian gondola gives the episode a graceful visual centre. Travel, culture and ordinary knowledge drift through the ladder rather less serenely, because Millionaire remains one of the few places where a pleasant boat ride can become an exam question.

s04e09.description: Stephen Hawking lends the episode some formidable scientific gravity. Cosmology and popular knowledge meet in a broad ladder that reminds everyone how comforting famous names are right up until the question asks for one precise fact about them.

s04e10.description: Crossing the Rubicon supplies history, metaphor and irreversible decision-making in one useful phrase. It is almost suspiciously appropriate for Millionaire, where every answer eventually becomes its own tiny river with no convenient bridge back.
